topic_en: Rust String vs &str: what is a slice

xhs.title: Rust 为什么有两种字符串？
xhs.body:
第 9 课：String 和 &str
String：拥有文字，放在堆上，能改能变长
&str：字符串切片，只借一段来看（起点 + 长度）
切片也是借用，切片还在用，原字符串就不能改
函数参数优先写 &str，字面量和 &String 都能传
考考你：let s = "hi"; s.push('!'); 能编译吗？ 评论区告诉我～

tiktok.body: Why does Rust have two string types? String owns its text; &str just borrows a slice of it. Quick quiz: let s = "hi"; s.push('!');  Does it compile? Comment your answer.

linkedin.title: Rust has two string types. Here is the difference.
linkedin.body:
String owns its text on the heap, so it can grow and change.
&str is a string slice: a borrowed view, just a pointer plus a length.
Because a slice is a borrow, the compiler won't let you change the String while the slice is in use.
That's why function parameters usually take &str: literals and &String both fit.
Quick quiz: let s = "hi"; s.push('!');  Does it compile? Answer in the comments.

quiz.q_zh: let s = "hi"; s.push('!'); 能编译吗？
quiz.q_en: let s = "hi"; s.push('!');  Does it compile?
quiz.answer_zh: 答案：不能。"hi" 是 &str，只读的字符串切片，没有 push。要改就用 let mut s = String::from("hi")。
quiz.answer_en: Answer: no. "hi" is a &str, a read-only string slice with no push. Use let mut s = String::from("hi") instead.
